cards.explanation: The answer is that He drives them all out. Jesus doesn't ease into this one. Matthew says He drove out all who were buying and selling there. I chase one runaway sprinkle across my counter and need a whole afternoon to recover, so I'm impressed.

The answer is False. Those tables did not stay put. Matthew says He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves. I couldn't knock over a cooling rack without three apologies.

The answer is prayer. Jesus declares, "It is written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer.’…" Prayer is what He says that house is meant to be. Then He says they are making it "a den of robbers."

The answer is a den of robbers. Jesus says to them, "But you are making it ‘a den of robbers.’…" He sets a house of prayer right beside a den of robbers, and the two pictures couldn't be further apart. That's some serious contrast, friends.

The answer is True. Matthew 21:14 says the blind and the lame came to Him at the temple, and He healed them. The same passage that has Him driving out buyers and sellers has the blind and the lame coming to Him. That's quite a turn in a few verses.

The answer is indignant. Matthew says the chief priests and scribes were indignant. That's when they saw the wonders Jesus performed and the children shouting in the temple courts. Same sights, and indignant is the word Matthew gives.

The answer is True. When the chief priests and scribes ask, "Do You hear what these children are saying?" Jesus answers, "Yes." Then He asks them a question of His own about what they've never read. Loud children are hard to miss, and I speak from experience with loud things in my bakery.
The answer is praise. Jesus says, "…‘From the mouths of children and infants You have ordained praise.’" The word is praise. He names children and infants as the mouths it comes from.
The answer is Bethany. Matthew says Jesus went out of the city to Bethany, where He spent the night. He left the leaders and the courts behind. Then in the morning He's heading back to the city.
The answer is nothing but leaves. Matthew says Jesus found nothing on the fig tree except leaves. He was hungry when He went up to it. Leaves were all there was.
The answer is that the tree withers at once. Jesus says, "May you never bear fruit again!" and Matthew says immediately the tree withered. No waiting around for a few weeks. It happened right then.
The answer is False. That's not what the disciples ask. They marvel and ask, "How did the fig tree wither so quickly?" They want to know how it happened so fast. That's all they ask.
The answer is doubt. Jesus says, "if you have faith and do not doubt, not only will you do what was done to the fig tree…" (Matthew 21:21). Faith and no doubt go together there. Doubt is the word.

The answer is this mountain. Jesus says, "…even if you say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ it will happen." A mountain is a whole lot bigger than a fig tree. He's the one who said it, so that's the picture we get.
The answer is True. Jesus says, "If you believe, you will receive whatever you ask for in prayer." That's how He ends His answer to the disciples. A promise about prayer, right at the close.
